topics.topic: Ownership and enforcement of INV-027 derived-value recomputation
questions: Which decision and module own INV-027's recomputation rule, including recomputation after budget-version activation?

Which module owns and enforces the schema-wide prohibition on stored derived values and the recomputation requirement after writes to expenses, progress, payments, plans and budget-version activation, when A18 is primarily owned by budget_management but expense_repository and project_tracking_repository are not its consumers?

quotes:
A15, A21 (derivation), A27 and the view part of A5: the viewer project list,
the project overview with its project and availability (Factory
`d2c4511ea119`), budget, expense, progress and payment views with their
orderings, and explicit unavailable values.
Read composition, projection, ordering and formula sequencing.
- hidden mechanism: read-time projection of owning records into views

INV-027: no table
  stores a value of a derived view (a total or aggregate; an import's
  content fingerprint is not one), reading the views writes nothing, and
  after every write of an owning record (inclusion, allocations, progress,
  payment, plan, budget-version activation) the next read equals a
  recomputation from the stored rows.
judgement.why: A21 and derived_views own read-time derivation, and INV-027 expressly requires the next read after every listed write, including activation, to recompute from owning rows rather than consume a cached aggregate.

topics.topic: Ownership of CLK-002 viewer-entry monotonic-clock rules
questions: Which module owns and enforces one monotonic reading per viewer-entry request, non-persistence, and the prohibition on mixing it with wall-clock values?

Does system_clock own CLK-002's one-reading-per-viewer-entry and rate-limit-window behavior, or does transport_guard own it, given that system_clock explicitly must not own how many readings an operation takes or the rate-limit window?

quotes:
- CLK-002: elapsed durations are measured only through the clock source's
  monotonic reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request; they
  are used within one process, never persisted,
  and never compared with or mixed into wall-clock values. Owner: the
  clock source.

When an operation reads the time, how many readings it takes, which instant
it reuses, any comparison, TTL arithmetic, storage or ordering of a reading,
and the rate-limit window.
judgement.divergence: The clock source owns and enforces the single per-request reading and rate-limit use, or transport_guard owns that behavior while system_clock merely returns one reading per call; a viewer at the window boundary notices admission versus refusal.
judgement.why: CLK-002 assigns the per-request and rate-window behavior to the clock source while the system_clock module expressly excludes those same responsibilities.

  are used within one process, never persisted,

When an operation reads the time, how many readings it takes, which instant
it reuses, any comparison, TTL arithmetic, storage or ordering of a reading,
and the rate-limit window.
bases.rests_on:
- the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per request of a
  clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. It measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of
  A25 only; a reading is never stored, never turned into an instant and
  never ordered against a persisted record.

unsupported_sides:
- CLK-002: elapsed durations are measured only through the clock source's
  monotonic reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request; they
  are used within one process, never persisted,
  and never compared with or mixed into wall-clock values. Owner: the
  clock source.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry request arrives at the boundary of its rate-limit window while the monotonic clock advances.
events: The viewer submits an entry request.
`transport_guard` evaluates the viewer-entry rate limit and obtains elapsed time from `system_clock`.
outcomes: The clock-source-owned rule supplies one elapsed reading for the whole request, so the attempt is evaluated consistently on one side of the boundary.

The transport guard may make multiple calls because system_clock owns only one reading per call, allowing parts of the decision to fall on opposite sides of the boundary and changing admission to refusal or refusal to admission.
basis:
The public API lives under `/api`, stripped by the deployment proxy. The
service answers only on its trusted hosts (at least one, no wildcard at any
position); CORS is off when its allowlist is empty, and an allowed origin is
never a wildcard. Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime
settings before expensive work; viewer entry attempts are rate limited per
client network address and route, with bounded memory and a concealed answer,
the address read only from the connection, never from a forwarded header,
cookie or secret.

A25 at the request boundary: one middleware that reads each path without
the `/api` prefix (stripped by the deployment proxy, A25; a path still
carrying it is read the same way), admits only trusted hosts, checks the origin of viewer sign-out, bounds the
body, rate-limits viewer entry per client address and route, sets the
security and `no-store` headers and writes one redacted log line.

questions: Who owns A28's per-operation one-reading, instant-reuse, comparison, TTL, supplied-time normalization and elapsed-window rules, since the primary owner is forbidden to own them and the consumer modules do not name their respective A28 parts in their Owns sections?

topics.topic: Ownership and sharing of the single wall-clock instant across authorization and mutation
questions: For a project-scoped use case whose authorization_guard checks session expiry and whose owning module writes event timestamps, which module takes the operation's single wall reading, and how is that instant shared between the guard and the mutation?

judgement.why: This is the same request-wide versus independently owned operation-clock question already decided by P13, and no cited clock passage has changed.

precedent.topic: Wall-clock read scope and ownership across an HTTP request and non-HTTP operations
quotes: _authorize_project_operation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

correct_expense: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

append_audit: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
precedent.why: State 7 explicitly requires one utc_now call independently in the authorization operation, the owning correction operation, and the audit append operation, so no request-wide clock acquisition or propagation is required.

questions: Which module owns validation and conversion of source-supplied approved_at, published_at, confirmed_at, photo_date and service-credential expires_at into offset-naive UTC while preserving the instant, given that models owns no behavior beyond closed-choice validation and system_clock must not own storage?

of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are

persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling

judgement.divergence: snapshot_import converts an offset-aware publication to UTC before removing its offset, preserving the instant, or merely removes the offset and preserves the wall reading; the producer and staff comparing snapshot chronology notice 10:00 versus 12:00.
judgement.why: The texts require instant-preserving offset-naive storage but do not assign normalization consistently: A28 is primarily assigned to system_clock, system_clock may not own storage, and snapshot_import owns unspecified canonicalization.

topics.topic: Whether missing progress becomes None now or remains zero until regeneration
questions: Does State 3 specify the new `None` behavior now, or preserve the accepted service's zero until regeneration?

quotes: - INV-044: remaining materials show overspend as negative values, never clamped or hidden; missing data is presented explicitly, never replaced by zero unless zero is confirmed: a section without a progress record reads completion_percent None and completed_work_value None
judgement.why: The normative invariant already requires None for both fields; the statement that the running service returns zero only records code awaiting regeneration and does not preserve zero as the design behavior.
